Hollywood has a habit. Studios find a franchise that works, one audiences love, one that earned trust over years or decades, and then they quietly swap out what made it great for whatever ideology is trending in the writers room. The original film is still on your shelf. The characters still have the same names. But something fundamental has changed, and not for the better.

VirtueVigil ran the numbers. We scored both the original and the sequel using our Woke-Watch Scoring System, tracking traditional and woke elements by severity, authenticity, and narrative centrality. Every film on this list saw its woke score climb substantially from the original to the follow-up. In several cases, films that started as crowd-pleasing action or family entertainment ended up scoring as outright WOKE. The betrayal is real, and the data backs it up.

Ranked by the size of the woke score jump from original to sequel, here are the 10 worst offenders.

#1
Aquaman and the Lost Kingdom (2023) WOKE -12 WOKE +24 WOKE JUMP
Original: Aquaman (2018) scored +12 TRAD. The sequel scored -12 WOKE.
Franchise: DC Extended Universe | Genre: Superhero Action
The original Aquaman was a pulpy, fun adventure that leaned on Atlantean mythology, father-son honor, and Arthur Curry earning his throne through courage. It scored strongly traditional. The sequel abandoned that formula almost entirely. Climate change messaging took center stage, Aquaman's masculine confidence was dialed back, and the political content that critics flagged as heavy-handed was no accident. The woke score jumped 24 points from the first film to the second. This is the biggest single-franchise woke surge on this list.
Read the full VirtueVigil review
#2
MaXXXine (2024) WOKE -18 WOKE +21 WOKE JUMP
Original: X (2022) scored -5 WOKE. The sequel scored -18 WOKE.
Franchise: X / MaXXXine Horror Series | Genre: Slasher Horror
Ti West's X was a smart, stripped-down slasher that understood its genre and delivered genuine tension without a political agenda cluttering the frame. MaXXXine, the follow-up set in 1980s Hollywood, traded the Texas farmhouse atmosphere for a parade of culture war signaling. The woke score jumped 21 points. What started as lean horror became a film more interested in making statements than building dread. Conservative horror fans who enjoyed X should consider themselves warned.
Read the full VirtueVigil review
#3
The Little Mermaid (2023) WOKE -12 WOKE +20 WOKE JUMP
Original: The Little Mermaid (1989) estimated +10 TRAD. The live-action remake scored -12 WOKE.
Franchise: Disney Animation | Genre: Musical Fantasy
The 1989 original is one of the most beloved animated films ever made: a girl who wanted something different from the world she was born into, a sea witch villain, a prince, and songs that have not left the public consciousness in 35 years. The 2023 live-action version kept the basic plot and rewrote everything else. Race-swapped casting turned into a culture war flashpoint, Ariel's motivation was reframed around female autonomy rather than wonder, and the woke score landed at -12. A 20-point swing on a film every parent grew up with.
Read the full VirtueVigil review
#4
The Marvels (2023) WOKE -14 WOKE +18 WOKE JUMP
Iron Man (2008) scored +9 TRAD. The Marvels scored -14 WOKE.
Franchise: Marvel Cinematic Universe | Genre: Superhero Action
Iron Man launched the MCU with a cocky, charismatic hero built around earned competence, personal accountability, and unapologetic American confidence. Fifteen years and dozens of films later, The Marvels represented what the franchise had become: a film so focused on girl-boss optics and intersectional casting that it forgot to be entertaining. It holds the record for lowest domestic opening weekend for any MCU film. The woke score jumped 18 points from where it all began. Audiences noticed before the critics did.
Read the full VirtueVigil review
#5
Dune: Part Two (2024) WOKE LEAN -8 WOKE +11 WOKE JUMP
Dune: Part One (2021) scored +6 TRAD. The sequel scored -8 WOKE.
Franchise: Dune | Genre: Science Fiction / Epic
Dune: Part One was a methodical, visually stunning adaptation of Herbert's novel that played its politics largely straight: a young man discovering destiny, ancient houses in conflict, a desert people defending their home. Part Two swung harder on progressive messaging, with Chani's arc reframed to carry explicit anti-colonialist and anti-religious-manipulation themes that went beyond the source material. The woke score jumped 11 points. Denis Villeneuve made a technically brilliant film with an ideology the original novel did not endorse.
Read the full VirtueVigil review
#6
Joker: Folie a Deux (2024) WOKE LEAN -2 WOKE +11 WOKE JUMP
Joker (2019) scored +1 TRAD. The sequel scored -2 WOKE.
Franchise: DC / Joker | Genre: Psychological Crime Drama
The original Joker was a polarizing, morally complex character study of societal failure and individual collapse. Whatever its politics, it was a film that respected its audience enough to leave them unsettled and thinking. Joker: Folie a Deux replaced that tension with a musical format, Lady Gaga, and a courtroom drama that explicitly argued for the psychiatric deconstruction of personal responsibility. The woke score jumped 11 points. Audiences voted with their wallets: it lost more than $150 million at the box office.
Read the full VirtueVigil review
#7
Lilo & Stitch (2025) WOKE LEAN -6 WOKE +13 WOKE JUMP
Original: Lilo & Stitch (2002) estimated +12 TRAD. The live-action remake scored -6 WOKE.
Franchise: Disney Animation | Genre: Family / Sci-Fi Comedy
The 2002 original was a genuine family gem: two sisters in Hawaii, a found family built through chaos and love, and a blue alien learning what ohana means. It had heart, humor, and a message about belonging that did not require an agenda. The 2025 live-action remake shifted the emphasis toward identity and autonomy themes that felt grafted onto a film that worked precisely because it did not need them. The woke score jumped 13 points. Disney's live-action remake machine keeps delivering the same result.
Read the full VirtueVigil review
#8
Beetlejuice Beetlejuice (2024) WOKE LEAN -4 WOKE +13 WOKE JUMP
Original: Beetlejuice (1988) estimated +15 TRAD. The sequel scored -4 WOKE.
Franchise: Tim Burton / Beetlejuice | Genre: Comedy Horror Fantasy
The original Beetlejuice was a Tim Burton classic: anarchic, weird, funny, and completely disinterested in anything resembling a political agenda. It was just a ghost comedy with a deranged bio-exorcist and a family of lovable losers. Thirty-six years later, the sequel loaded up on progressive themes. The woke score jumped 13 points from where the franchise started. What was once a film that stood outside culture entirely became a film very much embedded in 2024's version of it.
Read the full VirtueVigil review
#9
Jurassic World Rebirth (2025) WOKE LEAN -4 WOKE +9 WOKE JUMP
Original: Jurassic Park (1993) scored +5 TRAD. Jurassic World Rebirth scored -4 WOKE.
Franchise: Jurassic Park / Jurassic World | Genre: Action / Sci-Fi Thriller
Jurassic Park was about dinosaurs eating people and the hubris of thinking you can control nature. It worked because it kept the message simple and let the spectacle do the talking. Jurassic World Rebirth, the franchise's latest reboot attempt, added progressive character frameworks and social commentary on top of the dinosaur action. The woke score jumped 9 points from the original. The franchise has been declining in both quality and values coherence since the 1993 original, and Rebirth continues the trend.
Read the full VirtueVigil review
#10
Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness (2022) WOKE LEAN -3 WOKE +8 WOKE JUMP
Original: Doctor Strange (2016) scored +9 TRAD. The sequel scored -3 WOKE.
Franchise: Marvel Cinematic Universe / Doctor Strange | Genre: Superhero / Horror
The original Doctor Strange was a classic Marvel origin story: an arrogant surgeon humbled by loss, forced to earn wisdom and power through discipline and sacrifice under a demanding mentor. It scored strongly traditional. The sequel featured a multiverse-hopping Scarlet Witch as the primary villain, with feminist undertones about the power of motherhood weaponized as rage, and progressive casting choices across the multiverse variants. The woke score jumped 8 points. Sam Raimi brought his horror craft to the sequel but could not hide the ideological drift.
Read the full VirtueVigil review

The pattern here is consistent. Hollywood finds a franchise audiences love, one that earned goodwill through craft and story. Then the sequel arrives, carrying twice the ideological weight at half the entertainment value. The data does not lie. Before you buy a ticket to the next installment of a franchise you grew up with, check its VirtueVigil score first.
